outcome: Proportion with obstetric hemorrhage (defined as quantitative blood loss ≥ 1000 mL)
cohort: 2232 patients who received intrapartum oxytocin for induction or augmentation of labor at a single medical center between 2018 and 2019.
finding: Intrapartum oxytocin exposure of 12 hours or more was associated with increased quantitative blood loss and odds of obstetric hemorrhage in vaginal deliveries but not in cesarean deliveries.
mod_finding: Intrapartum oxytocin exposure of 12 hours or more was associated with increased quantitative blood loss and odds of obstetric hemorrhage in vaginal deliveries, though not in cesarean deliveries.
